hazards.title: Synchronous Blocking SQLite Call in Async Event Loop
hazards.description: Calling synchronous `sqlite3.connect().execute()` inside `async def submit_job` blocks the entire asyncio event loop, causing request starvation (0 TPS throughput) under concurrency.
hazards.remedy: Use `aiosqlite` or offload blocking database operations via `await asyncio.to_thread(db.insert_job, job)`.

hazards.title: sqlite3.Connection Shared Across Threadpool Workers
hazards.description: SQLite connection instantiated without `check_same_thread=False` or separate per-thread instances. Triggers `sqlite3.ProgrammingError` when accessed by concurrent threads.
hazards.remedy: Instantiate connections per thread or utilize an async connection pool.

idiomExplainers.concept: Asyncio Event Loop Non-Blocking Rule in Python
idiomExplainers.summary: Python's asyncio runs on a single operating system thread per process. Any synchronous I/O or sleep blocks all other concurrent requests.
idiomExplainers.whyItMatters: A 50ms synchronous SQLite write will delay 50 other pending API requests by 50ms each.
idiomExplainers.goRule: Never call synchronous disk or network I/O inside `async def` without `asyncio.to_thread()`.
idiomExplainers.codeExample:
import asyncio
import aiosqlite

async def async_insert(job):
    async with aiosqlite.connect('tasks.db') as db:
        await db.execute('INSERT INTO jobs (id) VALUES (?)', (job.id,))
        await db.commit()

invariants.invariant: All database operations inside async routes must be non-blocking
invariants.explanation: Synchronous sqlite3 call found in async route handler.

sourceFiles.main.py:
from fastapi import FastAPI
import sqlite3

app = FastAPI()

@app.post("/jobs")
async def submit_job(job_id: str, payload: str):
    # BUG: Synchronous blocking call inside async def
    conn = sqlite3.connect("tasks.db")
    conn.execute("INSERT INTO jobs VALUES (?, ?)", (job_id, payload))
    conn.commit()
    return {"status": "QUEUED"}
